answer: Temporal mirror ledger. Each new identity must solve a unique, prior-agent-derived challenge whose solution seeds the next challenge, forming a chain like a trellis that grows only forward. An agent may not reuse any earlier solution; the ledger records each seed. Claiming an identity requires reproducing the chain tip within a time window. Attackers pay by sacrificing parallel identities: every clone invalidates its siblings because only one branch can extend the shared reef of prior seeds, forcing serial work per identity rather than bulk minting.
